plan.melodySummary: The famous theme migrates across the ensemble — beginning warmly in the French Horn, blossoming into Violin 1 for the soaring statements, dipping into the Cello for a tender interior, and returning triumphantly to the full violins for the climax before a gentle resolution. The dynamic arc rises from an intimate mezzo-piano through espressivo swells to a fortissimo high point at mm.21-24, then settles back into a hushed, glowing close.

sections.label: Phrase A — First Statement
sections.notes: Sing the theme !mp! espressivo, rounded and legato with a slight lingering on the phrase-end half notes; shape each two-bar arch with a gentle hairpin.

sections.label: Phrase B — Answering Interior
sections.notes: Take up the melody !mf! with a warm singing tone, dotted lean into the FG turns; ease back to !mp! at m.16 to prepare the octave lift.

sections.label: Phrase C — Octave Rise & Development
sections.notes: Ascend into the upper octave building !mf!→!f!→!ff!, broad and heroic through mm.21-24; give full bow weight to the climactic D at m.24 as the arrangement's peak.

sections.label: Phrase D — Tender Interior
sections.notes: Draw the descending line !p! dolce on rich tenor strings, molto espressivo with a subtle rubato and a suspension-tinged sigh into m.28.

sections.label: Phrase E — Final Resolution
sections.notes: Restate !mf! then bloom to a warm !f! at m.31, broadening with a ritardando; let the final whole note ring and diminuendo to !p! for a glowing close.

Violin 1.instruction: Chief soaring voice: espressivo singing tone with expressive vibrato, dotted phrasing and phrase-end lingering. Drops to shimmering repeated-chord accompaniment in mm.1-8 and to a soft high pedal-bass role in mm.25-28. Shape every phrase with hairpins.

Violin 2.instruction: Flowing inner harmony throughout — gently repeated chords and rising arpeggios with chromatic suspensions resolving downward. Stay one dynamic step under the melody carrier at all times, swelling only within the collective hairpins.

Clarinet.instruction: Lyrical chromatic countermelody and inner-voice color; weave secondary-dominant leading tones and suspensions between the given chords. In mm.9-16 provides flowing eighth-note motion; always espressivo but never covering the melody.

French Horn.instruction: Opens the theme !mp! warm and noble, legato and rounded. Afterward becomes a sustaining harmonic anchor and adds a horn-call countermelody in mm.29-32; keep sustained notes softer than whichever instrument leads.

Cello.instruction: Foundation in flowing arpeggiated bass lines with chromatic passing tones under the given harmonies. Steps into the spotlight for the tender interior mm.25-28 !p! molto espressivo, then returns to a resonant walking-arpeggio bass for the finale.
